elements.reason: The retrieved evidence does not include the manuscript’s abstract content, so it does not show an explicit statement that the report is a systematic review.

The retrieved evidence does not include abstract text specifying main inclusion and exclusion criteria.

Risk of bias/quality assessment methods are described in other sections, but no abstract text is retrieved showing this information.
Methods for presenting/synthesizing results are present in retrieved non-abstract sections, but the abstract evidence is not provided to confirm this item.

While numbers of studies/participants appear in retrieved Results sections, the retrieved evidence does not provide abstract text summarizing included studies/participants and relevant characteristics.
Main outcome results are reported in retrieved non-abstract Results text, but the abstract is not retrieved, so the PRISMA abstract requirement cannot be confirmed.
A pooled estimate with 95% CI is present in retrieved Results text (not shown as abstract). Since the criterion is for the abstract and no abstract text is retrieved, this cannot be confirmed.
Direction of effect/favored group is not confirmed in retrieved abstract text; no abstract evidence is provided.
No abstract text is retrieved describing limitations of the included evidence (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision).
No abstract text is retrieved providing a general interpretation and important implications.
Funding is mentioned in the Methods evidence, but the retrieved evidence does not include abstract text specifying the primary source of funding.
PROSPERO registration is reported in retrieved Methods/Search strategies text, but no abstract text is retrieved that provides the register name and registration number.
The retrieved evidence does not describe the current state of knowledge or important uncertainties regarding surgical site infection after cesarean section and its predictors in Ethiopia.
The retrieved evidence does not explain the importance and need for conducting the review.

Although PROSPERO registration and checking for duplication are mentioned, the retrieved evidence does not describe whether similar systematic reviews exist and does not explain the need for this review in relation to prior reviews (updates/replications with citations).
This review concerns prevalence and/or factors associated with SSI (observational studies/predictors) rather than an intervention with a proposed mechanism of action.

The retrieved evidence indicates the study synthesizes observational evidence on prevalence/predictors of SSI and does not describe a complex intervention or delivery context that would warrant a logic model.

elements.reason: The review objective/question is explicitly stated in the introduction/objective section.

elements.quote: Inclusion. This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs (case-control and cross-sectional study designs) were included in this SRMA.
elements.reason: Specifies eligibility study characteristics including setting (all regional state of Ethiopia), outcomes (prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors), and eligible study designs (observational; case-control and cross-sectional). However, follow-up requirements are not specified.

elements.quote: Both published articles and grey literatures published in English language from January 1 2013 to September 2023.
elements.reason: Report characteristics for eligibility are specified, including publication status (published and grey literature), language (English), and dissemination/time range (Jan 1 2013 to Sep 2023).
The evidence does not distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured versus exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

No rationales are provided for notable restrictions on study eligibility (e.g., language restriction or time window) in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: An appropriate and comprehensive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, Google Scholar, HINARI and Scopus was done since 2013. Furthermore, relevant articles found from grey literatures available on local shelves and institutional repositories were reviewed systematically. Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and key terms had been developed using different Boolean operators 'AND' and 'OR'. The following search terms were used: '(prevalence) OR (magnitude) OR (proportion) OR (epidemiology) OR (surgical site infection) OR (surgical site) OR (wound infection) AND (cesarean section) OR (cesarean delivery) OR (post cesarean section) AND (determinants) OR (associated factors) OR (risk factors) OR (predictors) AND (Ethiopia)'.

elements.quote: This SRMA has comprised of two main outcomes. The primary outcome was magnitude of SSI among women underwent cesarean section, which is defined as the proportion of women after cesarean section who fulfills the CDC criteria of surgical site definition within 30 days of post-partum and it could be at least one of the following: ( A superficial incisional , deep incisional or deep/organ SSI) . The secondary outcome was the determinants of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: The manuscript lists two outcome domains (primary: magnitude of SSI; secondary: determinants) and provides definitions/description for each.

elements.quote: Atotal of 6334 articles were found by using our search strategies: Google scholar, pub-med, Hinari, EMBASE, Scopus and Medline. After 1398 articles were removed for the reason of duplication, 4932 articles left. Then by reviewing their titles and abstracts, 4800 and 100 articles were removed respectively. Finally 32 full text papers were accessed and evaluated for the predefined inclusion criteria. Thus 13 more articles were excluded for the afore-mentioned reasons. Eventually, 19 articles were found eligible for inclusion in the final SRMA (Fig 1).
elements.reason: Reports the numbers identified (6334), removed for duplication (1398), screened (4932), excluded after title/abstract screening (4800 and 100), and full-text assessed/excluded (32 accessed; 13 excluded).

elements.quote: The pooled estimate of SSI in Ethiopia was 11.13% (95%CI, 9.2912.97%). Prolonged labor (AOR = 3.16, 95% CI; (2.14-4.68)), chorioamnionitis (AOR = 4.26, 95% CI; (1.99-8.91)), prolonged PROM (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI; (2.51-5.62)), repeated vaginal examination (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI; (2.45-5.88)), decreased hemoglobin level (AOR = 4.57, 95%CI; (3.16-6.60)), vertical skin incision (AOR = 3.09, 95% CI; (2.04-4.67)) and general anesthesia (AOR = 1.82, 95% CI (1.21-2.75)) are significantly associated with SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.

elements.quote: The result of this SRMA showed the overall pooled prevalence of SSI following cesarean section in Ethiopia was 11.13% with a 95% CI: (9.29, 12.97%), which is much higher than the global prevalence of 5.63% [40]. This result is consistent with a study conducted in Rwanda which is 10.9% [14]. However, this was lower than the study conducted in China [15], Jordan [41] and Ekiti state, Nigeria [13] reported 23.3%, 14.4% and 16.01% respectively. On the contrary, our study finding was much higher than the studies conducted in developed nations: Ireland [42], Poland [5], Estonia [10] and Egypt [43] reported 0.63%, 0.5%, 6.2% and 5.34% respectively.
elements.reason: The Discussion interprets the pooled prevalence by comparing it with global prevalence and multiple countries/regions and provides explanations for discrepancies, i.e., interpretation in the context of other relevant evidence.
